note: Part 9: the weapon in the hand. PD 1.9 draws no weapon on the hero; here the equipped weapon (or the thrown weapon a huntress or a rogue holds) is a second picture at the hand, frame by frame, in each of part 8's three facings.

sheet.row1: the trail of the blow (frame 14): column 0 side, 1 front, 2 back

place: the weapon cell's pixel (8, 8) goes on the hand's pixel of the hero frame, moved by the pose's (dx, dy); the side view mirrors the whole (angle a becomes 360 - a: the picture is flipped with the hero's); the grip pixel is clear, so the hand of the body shows round the handle
layer: front: drawn after the body and its hat (a hand on the costume, a raised blade over the hat); back: drawn before the body

anims.zap: poses[style][facing].hold: a wand zaps from the other hand, the weapon is held still
anims.throw: a thrown weapon that is the one in the hand: poses.throw.attack (gone from the hand from frame 14; the boomerang is back when it returns)
anims.other: every other animation: hold (its frames carry the hand)

styles.slash: swords, the axe, the glaive: raised behind, cut down across, a trail along the arc
styles.blunt: mace, war hammer, pickaxe: raised high, brought straight down
styles.stab: dagger, spear: drawn back, thrust along itself (at the camera from the front, away from it from behind)
styles.staff: quarterstaff: held upright, swung and jabbed
styles.throw: stones, darts, shuriken, tomahawk, javelin, boomerang: in the raised hand at 13, gone at 14
styles.fist: knuckles: on the fist, the punch is PD's own
